raw_text: Several engine defects were "silent no-op" bugs: they produced plausible-looking but empty results instead of failing loudly. The index builder searched only the top-level directory, not nested subdirectories. It hid three of four domains and reported zero sessions when 53 existed; after the fix, a rebuild recovered all 88 inferences without spending any LLM tokens. The parity check between the fused logos path and the per-operator path exited successfully because it pointed at stale paths and treated missing files as skipped, not as errors. Once it was fixed, the check revealed a real difference between the two paths, such as sovereign versus tribal classifications. The broader lesson is that a check that cannot fail gives false confidence. Missing inputs should be errors, and a clean pass should be verified, not assumed.
